slides.title: Methods toolkit: from neurons to behavior
slides.body:
**Spatial + temporal scales** of measurement:

**Single neurons**:
- **Single-unit recording**: gold standard; electrode in/near neuron; spikes recorded. Hubel + Wiesel Nobel 1981 for V1 single-unit work.
- **Multi-electrode arrays** (Utah, Neuropixels): 100s-1000s of neurons simultaneously.
- **Calcium imaging** (2-photon microscopy): visualize 1000s of neurons in living animal; slower (~Hz) than electrophysiology.
- **Patch clamp**: intracellular recording; channel + synaptic studies.

**Mesoscale (humans + animals)**:
- **fMRI (BOLD)**: blood-flow proxy for neural activity. ~3-5 mm spatial; 2-3 sec temporal. Whole-brain.
- **EEG**: scalp electrodes; ms-temporal; cm-spatial. Cheap + portable.
- **MEG**: magnetic fields from neural currents. Better spatial than EEG.
- **NIRS**: near-IR; hemodynamics; portable.
- **ECoG**: electrodes on cortical surface; clinical patients (epilepsy); high resolution.
- **Stereo-EEG** (sEEG): depth electrodes; epilepsy patients.

**Causal manipulations**:
- **TMS (transcranial magnetic stimulation)**: induce transient activity in target region. Causal.
- **Optogenetics** (Deisseroth 2005+): light-activated channels in genetically-defined neurons. Animal models.
- **DREADDs**: chemogenetic; designer drugs.
- **Lesion studies + reversible inactivation** (e.g., muscimol): selective inactivation.
- **TES/tDCS**: transcranial electrical; mild + safer than TMS.

**Behavioral**:
- Psychophysics; RT + accuracy; eye-tracking; mouse-tracking; speech analysis.

**Modern combination**: multimodal acquisition for richer pictures.

slides.title: Multivariate + decoding methods
slides.body:
**Traditional fMRI analysis** (1990s-2000s): univariate, voxel-by-voxel. 'This voxel responds to faces.'

**Multivariate pattern analysis (MVPA)** (Haxby 2001+): pattern of activity across voxels carries information. Use ML classifiers to decode mental content.

**Common methods**:
- **Pattern classification**: SVM, logistic regression on multi-voxel patterns.
- **Representational similarity analysis (RSA)**: compare neural similarity matrices to model predictions.
- **Searchlight**: classify across moving window; find informative regions.
- **Encoding models**: predict neural response from stimulus features.

**Decoding successes**:
- Stimulus reconstruction from fMRI: Tang + Huth 2023 reconstructed continuous speech from fMRI BOLD!
- Visual reconstruction (Naselaris + Gallant): natural images from fMRI.
- Dream content decoding (Horikawa + Kamitani 2013).
- Affect + emotion decoding.
- Memory content decoding (sometimes).

**BCI + decoding**:
- Motor decoding for prosthetics (BrainGate, Neuralink, Synchron).
- Speech decoding (Chang + others 2021-23): cortical recordings → real-time speech.
- Sensory restoration: cochlear implants, retinal implants, somatosensory.

**Modeling neural representations**:
- Compare brain representations to artificial neural networks (CNN, transformer).
- ANN-brain correspondence (Yamins + DiCarlo 2014; Schrimpf 2020).
- Brain-aligned objectives in ML training.
- Foundation models predict neural responses across many tasks (Schrimpf 2021).

**Modern frontiers**:
- High-density Neuropixels probes.
- Wearable EEG + fMRI hardware.
- Real-time analysis + neurofeedback.
- BCI + AI integration.

slides.title: Clinical applications + AI neuroscience
slides.body:
**Computational psychiatry**: applies cognitive-neuroscience methods to mental disorders. Uses computational models (DDM, RL, Bayesian) as biomarkers.

**Diagnostic + treatment**:
- **Deep brain stimulation (DBS)**: Parkinson's (subthalamic nucleus), essential tremor (Vim thalamus), dystonia, OCD, depression (some).
- **Repetitive TMS (rTMS)**: FDA-approved for depression (2008), OCD, smoking cessation.
- **Closed-loop neurostimulation**: NeuroPace RNS for refractory epilepsy.
- **MR-guided focused ultrasound**: noninvasive tremor + tumor targeting.

**Brain-machine interfaces (BMI)**:
- **Restoring function**: motor (BrainGate, Neuralink), communication (speech-BCI, Stentrode), vision (Argus retinal implant).
- **Augmentation**: long-term goal; ethical debates.
- **Modern**: ALS + tetraplegia patients controlling robotic arms, mouse cursors, communicate.

**AI + neuroscience cross-pollination**:
- Deep learning inspired by visual cortex hierarchical processing.
- Reinforcement learning + dopamine: TD-learning theory ↔ neural mechanism.
- Attention mechanisms (transformers) inspired by selective attention.
- Predictive processing (Friston): both brain + LLM architectures.
- Decoding language from brain activity (Tang + Huth 2023).
- Cortical activity → speech in real-time (Chang lab UCSF; recent ALS patient communicating).
- Foundation models as cognitive theory.

**Modern challenges + frontiers**:
- Whole-brain connectivity (Allen Brain Atlas + Human Connectome Project).
- Generative models of cognition + behavior.
- Multi-omic + multi-modal neuroscience.
- Ethics: brain data privacy, BMI autonomy, neurorights laws (Chile 2021).

Cognitive neuroscience: foundational both for understanding mind + for translational medicine + AI alignment.

question.question: Decode visual category from fMRI activity
question.goal: Plan an MVPA experiment to decode 'faces vs scenes' from fMRI activity.

acceptedAnswers: block + event-related; balanced face + scene blocks

steps.reveal: Block + event-related design: present face stimuli + scene stimuli in randomized blocks; many trials per category (>50). Fixation baseline. Counter-balance order.

acceptedAnswers: fusiform face area + parahippocampal place area

steps.reveal: ROIs: FFA (fusiform face area) — face-selective; PPA (parahippocampal place area) — scene-selective. Also: searchlight (moving window across whole brain) to find informative regions beyond ROIs.

acceptedAnswers: SVM or logistic regression with cross-validation

steps.reveal: Train SVM or logistic regression on voxel activity patterns to discriminate face vs scene trials. Use leave-one-run-out cross-validation: train on subset of runs, test on held-out run. Repeat across all runs. Report mean decoding accuracy + confidence interval.

acceptedAnswers: compare to chance via permutation tests; report effect sizes

steps.reveal: Compare decoding accuracy to chance (50% for 2-way) via permutation test (shuffle labels + recompute many times → null distribution). Report effect sizes + corrected p-values (FWE or FDR across multiple comparisons). Decoding accuracy in FFA + PPA typically 70-90% for face/scene; well above chance. RSA can compare representational structures.

question.question: Match each neuroscience method to its primary trade-off.
question.explanation: Method trade-offs: fMRI/PET high spatial + low temporal; EEG/MEG high temporal + low spatial; TMS/optogenetics causal manipulation; single-unit/Neuropixels spike-level. Multimodal combinations (e.g., simultaneous EEG-fMRI) leverage strengths. Modern: fast fMRI (TR <500 ms), multi-echo, accelerated imaging. Single-cell methods: Neuropixels (1000s channels), 2-photon imaging.

question.question: Why have BCI + neural decoders progressed so rapidly in 2020-2024?
options: Combination: (1) Better electrodes (Utah arrays maintained; Neuralink threads with 1024+ channels; Synchron Stentrode); (2) Deep-learning decoders (transformers + RNNs replace older linear methods); (3) Larger datasets; (4) Improved surgical + neurosurgical techniques; (5) Investment + commercial pressure (NeuraLink, Synchron, BlackRock, Paradromics, Precision Neuroscience); (6) FDA breakthrough designations expediting. Recent: ALS + tetraplegia patients communicating via cortical speech BCI (Chang lab + Stanford); cursor + robotic-arm control; mental-imagery decoding (Tang + Huth 2023).
question.explanation: BCI progress 2020-2024: better electrodes + deep-learning decoders + data + surgical + investment. Recent: ALS patients communicating via cortical speech BCI (Chang lab UCSF 2023 + Stanford 2023; Pancho Diaz; Casey Harrell); cursor/arm control (BrainGate, Neuralink); imagery decoding (Tang + Huth 2023 fMRI). Companies: Neuralink (Musk; 4+ implants by 2024), Synchron (FDA breakthrough), BlackRock, Paradromics, Precision. Modern: explosive growth; ethical + regulatory frameworks catching up.

slides.workedSolution: BCI 2020-2024: better electrodes (Neuralink, Synchron, Utah persist), deep-learning decoders (transformers), large data, improved surgery, investment + commercial pressure (Neuralink, Synchron, BlackRock, Paradromics, Precision), FDA breakthrough. Recent: ALS patients speech BCI (Chang UCSF 2023, Stanford 2023); cursor/arm control; mental-imagery decoding (Tang + Huth 2023). Ethical + regulatory frameworks catching up.

question.question: Drag to typical fMRI BOLD temporal resolution (in sec).
question.explanation: Standard fMRI: ~2-3 sec temporal resolution (TR). Multiband + accelerated: ~0.5-1 sec. Slower than neural activity (ms scale) but spans seconds-min processes. Spatial: 2-3 mm. Limitations: hemodynamic delay ~6 sec; spatial blur ~5 mm.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain how cognitive neuroscience has reshaped our understanding of mind.
question.rubric: Mentions: 50 years of cognitive neuroscience integrated psychology + neuroscience + computer science. Established: mind has multiple specialized systems (perception, attention, memory, language, executive); brain regions have specialized functions (V1, FFA, hippocampus, PFC, etc.) coordinated in networks; cognition is computational + neural simultaneously (Marr's levels); plasticity throughout life; cognitive biases + System-1/2 architecture. Methods (fMRI, EEG, single-cell, optogenetics, computational models) provide windows into mind. Clinical: psychiatric + neurological disorders increasingly understood as computational dysfunctions; better targeting. AI: cognitive science + deep learning cross-pollinate; foundation models illuminate cognition. Modern: BCI + neural decoding enable communication for ALS + tetraplegia; mental-imagery reconstruction; foundation models as cognitive theory. Concludes: cognitive neuroscience is one of the most active + consequential scientific fields; understanding the mind is humanity's most important question; clinical + AI implications profound. Major themes: hierarchy, prediction, learning, control, plasticity, integration of streams.
